name: Every operator and verifier list change is audited
summary: admin.py operators add|remove and verifiers add|remove take --actor OPERATOR (who makes the change) and --reason TEXT (at most 400 characters; blank refused). A change that really changes a list appends one entry - at, operator, list, actor, change (add or remove), reason - to the runtime-level authority-changes.audit.json beside deployment.private.json: schema_version 1, mode 0600, newest 200 kept, written under the deployment lock and BEFORE the configuration, so a crash leaves an entry with no change rather than a change with no entry. The read-only admin.py authority-changes command prints it, writes nothing and never creates the file. A call without the flags keeps working (the office wrapper coord.sh runs the bare form): it still records the change, with operator and/or reason null, and prints one stderr sentence naming what to add. The recorded --actor is a record, not a grant: the four commands check no allowlist. A hand-damaged audit is refused by all five commands before anything is written, never read as an empty history. Downgrade: an older kit neither reads nor writes the file, so it loses no function and records no new entries.
